Amazon S3 Files lets you mount an S3 bucket as an NFS file system. Learn the prerequisites before starting a walkthrough.

import { CardGrid, LinkCard, Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Amazon S3 Files** mounts an S3 bucket as an NFS file system inside EC2, ECS Fargate, and Lambda — giving your applications a familiar POSIX file-system interface backed by durable object storage.

This site contains two types of walkthroughs:

- **CLI** — step-by-step AWS CLI commands for EC2 and Lambda. Each section is self-contained and includes its own setup and teardown.
- **Terraform** — `terraform apply` examples for EC2, ECS Fargate, and Lambda using the [terraform-aws-s3-files](https://github.com/jajera/terraform-aws-s3-files) modules.

---

## Prerequisites

Review these requirements before starting any walkthrough. They apply to both the CLI and Terraform sections.

### S3 bucket

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Versioning** | Must be enabled — S3 Files uses versioning to synchronise changes between the file system and the bucket. File system creation fails if versioning is off. |
| **Encryption** | SSE-S3 (`AES256`) or SSE-KMS only. SSE-C (customer-provided keys) and DSSE-KMS are **not supported**. New buckets default to SSE-S3, which works without extra configuration. |

### IAM — two roles required

S3 Files uses exactly two IAM roles:

| Role | Service principal | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **File system role** | `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com` | S3 Files assumes this role to read/write your bucket and manage EventBridge sync rules. The trust policy `aws:SourceArn` must use `arn:aws:s3files:…` — **not** `arn:aws:elasticfilesystem:…`. |
| **Compute role** | `ec2.amazonaws.com` / `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` / `lambda.amazonaws.com` | Your compute resource assumes this role to mount the file system and read objects from S3. |

### Network

NFS port **2049 TCP** must be open between the compute security group and the mount target security group. Mount targets run in the same VPC as your compute resources, one per Availability Zone.

### AWS CLI (for CLI walkthroughs)

The `aws s3files` subcommand requires **AWS CLI v2.34.26 or newer**. Versions v2.34.23 and earlier do not include the `s3files` namespace and return `Found invalid choice 's3files'`. AWS CLI v1 (e.g. installed via `pip install awscli`) never includes S3 Files.

```bash frame="terminal"
aws --version          # must show 2.34.26 or newer
aws s3files help       # must list s3files subcommands
```

### Terraform (for Terraform walkthroughs)

| Requirement | Minimum version |
| --- | --- |
| Terraform | 1.5 |
| AWS provider (`hashicorp/aws`) | 6.40 |

<Aside type="note">
  The Terraform AWS provider added native S3 Files resources (`aws_s3files_*`) in version **6.40**. Earlier versions do not include these resources.
</Aside>

### Platform constraints

| Platform | Constraint |
| --- | --- |
| EC2 | Requires `amazon-efs-utils` v3.0.0+ for the `mount -t s3files` helper |
| ECS | **Fargate and Managed Instances only** — EC2 launch type is not supported |
| Lambda | **Access point required** — Lambda cannot mount by file system ID alone |

## What this example does

This example provisions:

- An S3 bucket (versioning + SSE-S3 enabled)
- An S3 Files file system and mount targets in each provided subnet
- IAM roles (file system role + EC2 instance profile)
- Security groups (compute → mount target on NFS port 2049)
- An Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance with `amazon-efs-utils` installed and the file system mounted at `/mnt/s3files`

Access to the instance is through **SSM Session Manager** — no SSH key pair or bastion host is needed.

<Steps>

1. **Confirm prerequisites.**

   | Requirement | Minimum version |
   | --- | --- |
   | Terraform | 1.5 |
   | AWS provider | 6.40 |
   | AWS CLI | 2.34.26 (for `aws ssm start-session`) |

   Install the Session Manager plugin if not already present:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws ssm start-session --version
   ```

   If the command is not found, follow the [AWS Session Manager plugin installation guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-working-with-install-plugin.html).

2. **Clone the example.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   git clone https://github.com/jajera/terraform-aws-s3-files.git
   cd terraform-aws-s3-files/examples/ec2
   ```

   The example directory contains:

   <FileTree>
   - examples/ec2/
     - main.tf
     - terraform.tfvars.example
     - terraform.tfvars _(you create this)_
   </FileTree>

3. **Create `terraform.tfvars`.**

   Copy the example file and set your VPC and subnet IDs:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
   ```

   Edit `terraform.tfvars`:

   ```hcl
   vpc_id     = "vpc-0123456789abcdef0"
   subnet_ids = ["subnet-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "subnet-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"]

   # Optional overrides (defaults shown):
   # aws_region         = "ap-southeast-6"
   # instance_type      = "t3.micro"
   # bucket_name        = null   # auto-generated: s3files-demo-<random>
   # bucket_force_destroy = true
   ```

   | Variable | Default | Required | Description |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `vpc_id` | — | yes | VPC for mount targets and EC2 instance |
   | `subnet_ids` | — | yes | Subnets for mount targets (one per AZ recommended) |
   | `instance_subnet_id` | first `subnet_ids` entry | no | Subnet for the EC2 instance |
   | `aws_region` | `ap-southeast-6` | no | AWS region |
   | `instance_type` | `t3.micro` | no | EC2 instance type |
   | `bucket_name` | auto-generated | no | Leave `null` to use `s3files-demo-<random>` |
   | `bucket_force_destroy` | `true` | no | Allow destroy even when bucket contains objects |

4. **Initialise and apply.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   terraform init
   terraform plan
   terraform apply
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     `terraform apply` creates the file system, waits for mount targets to become available, and launches the EC2 instance. The user data script installs `amazon-efs-utils` and mounts the file system. Allow 3–5 minutes for the instance to reach a ready state after the apply completes.
   </Aside>

   When apply finishes, note the outputs:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   terraform output
   ```

   Key outputs:

   | Output | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | `instance_id` | EC2 instance ID (`i-…`) |
   | `file_system_id` | S3 Files file system ID |
   | `bucket_name` | Backing S3 bucket name |
   | `ami_id` | Amazon Linux 2023 AMI used |

5. **Connect via SSM Session Manager.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws ssm start-session \
     --target "$(terraform output -raw instance_id)" \
     --region ap-southeast-6
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     If the session fails immediately with `TargetNotConnected`, the SSM agent may still be starting. Wait 60 seconds and retry. The instance must reach SSM before user data completes.
   </Aside>

6. **Verify the mount.**

   Inside the SSM session:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   df -h /mnt/s3files
   ls -la /mnt/s3files
   ```

   Write a file and confirm it appears in S3:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   echo "hello from terraform ec2" > /mnt/s3files/test.txt
   cat /mnt/s3files/test.txt
   ```

   Exit the session when done:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   exit
   ```

7. **Tear down.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   terraform destroy
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     `bucket_force_destroy = true` (the default) means `terraform destroy` deletes the bucket and all its objects, including all S3 versioning history. Set it to `false` before apply if you need to preserve the bucket.
   </Aside>

</Steps>

## What this example does

This example provisions:

- An S3 bucket (versioning + SSE-S3 enabled)
- An S3 Files file system and mount targets in each provided subnet
- An S3 Files access point at `/lambda` (UID/GID 1000, required for Lambda)
- IAM roles (file system role + Lambda execution role with VPC access)
- Security groups (compute → mount target on NFS port 2049)
- A CloudWatch log group for the Lambda function
- A Python 3.14 Lambda function that lists `/mnt/s3files`

<Aside type="caution">
  Lambda **requires an access point** — it cannot mount an S3 Files file system by file system ID alone. The example creates one automatically at root directory `/lambda` with POSIX UID/GID 1000.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm prerequisites.**

   | Requirement | Minimum version |
   | --- | --- |
   | Terraform | 1.5 |
   | AWS provider | 6.40 |
   | archive provider | 2.4 |
   | AWS CLI | 2.34.26 |

   Confirm the CLI version:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws --version
   ```

   The subnets you provide must have outbound internet access (via NAT Gateway) or VPC interface endpoints for Lambda to reach the Lambda service, CloudWatch Logs, and S3. Private subnets with a NAT Gateway are the most common setup.

2. **Clone the example.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   git clone https://github.com/jajera/terraform-aws-s3-files.git
   cd terraform-aws-s3-files/examples/lambda
   ```

   <FileTree>
   - examples/lambda/
     - main.tf
     - terraform.tfvars.example
     - terraform.tfvars _(you create this)_
   </FileTree>

   The Lambda function code is generated inline by Terraform using the `archive` provider — no separate function file is needed.

3. **Create `terraform.tfvars`.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
   ```

   Edit `terraform.tfvars`:

   ```hcl
   vpc_id     = "vpc-0123456789abcdef0"
   subnet_ids = ["subnet-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "subnet-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"]

   # Optional overrides (defaults shown):
   # aws_region         = "ap-southeast-6"
   # log_retention_days = 7
   # bucket_name        = null   # auto-generated: s3files-demo-<random>
   # bucket_force_destroy = true
   ```

   | Variable | Default | Required | Description |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `vpc_id` | — | yes | VPC for mount targets and Lambda ENIs |
   | `subnet_ids` | — | yes | Subnets for mount targets and Lambda (must have NAT or VPC endpoints) |
   | `aws_region` | `ap-southeast-6` | no | AWS region |
   | `log_retention_days` | `7` | no | CloudWatch log retention period in days |
   | `bucket_name` | auto-generated | no | Leave `null` to use `s3files-demo-<random>` |
   | `bucket_force_destroy` | `true` | no | Allow destroy even when bucket contains objects |

4. **Initialise and apply.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   terraform init
   terraform plan
   terraform apply
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     `terraform apply` creates all S3 Files infrastructure, the access point, and the Lambda function. The archive provider packages the inline Python handler into `lambda.zip` locally. Allow 3–5 minutes for mount targets to become available before invoking the function.
   </Aside>

   When apply finishes, note the outputs:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   terraform output
   ```

   Key outputs:

   | Output | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | `lambda_function_name` | Lambda function name |
   | `file_system_id` | S3 Files file system ID |
   | `access_point_arn` | ARN of the S3 Files access point |
   | `bucket_name` | Backing S3 bucket name |

5. **Invoke the function.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda invoke \
     --function-name "$(terraform output -raw lambda_function_name)" \
     --region ap-southeast-6 \
     --payload '{}' \
     response.json \
   && cat response.json
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     The first invocation may return a cold-start error if the mount target is still provisioning. Wait 2–3 minutes and retry if you receive a timeout or mount-related error.
   </Aside>

6. **Verify the response.**

   Expected response body:

   ```json
   {"statusCode": 200, "body": "[]"}
   ```

   The empty list `[]` is correct — the file system is empty at this point. Write a file via the S3 CLI and invoke again to see it appear:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3 cp /dev/stdin \
     "s3://$(terraform output -raw bucket_name)/lambda/hello.txt" \
     --content-type text/plain \
     --region ap-southeast-6 <<< "hello from terraform lambda"

   aws lambda invoke \
     --function-name "$(terraform output -raw lambda_function_name)" \
     --region ap-southeast-6 \
     --payload '{}' \
     response.json \
   && cat response.json
   ```

   The response body should now list `['hello.txt']`.

7. **Tear down.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   terraform destroy
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     `bucket_force_destroy = true` (the default) means `terraform destroy` deletes the bucket and all its objects. Set it to `false` before apply if you need to preserve the bucket contents.
   </Aside>

</Steps>

## Overview

This page launches a **t3.micro Amazon Linux 2023** instance into the same VPC as the S3 Files mount targets, attaches the compute instance profile created in [IAM](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/iam/), and connects using **SSM Session Manager** — no key pair or public IP required.

<Aside type="note">
  The instance subnet must be in the same Availability Zone as at least one mount target, but it can be a **public or NAT-routed subnet** so SSM can reach the AWS APIs. Mount targets can stay on private subnets.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell. Resolve `COMPUTE_SG_ID` by name if the variable is not still set.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export VPC_ID=vpc-0123456789abcdef0   # ← replace with your VPC ID

   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket      # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}

   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --bucket "$BUCKET_ARN" \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)
   echo "FS_ID=$FS_ID"

   export COMPUTE_SG_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups \
     --filters \
       "Name=group-name,Values=s3files-ec2-compute-sg" \
       "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' \
     --output text)
   echo "COMPUTE_SG_ID=$COMPUTE_SG_ID"
   ```

   `FS_ID` must be `fs-…` and `COMPUTE_SG_ID` must be `sg-…`. If either is `None`, complete the [Setup](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/bucket/) pages first.

2. **Add HTTPS egress to the compute security group.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   SSM Session Manager requires outbound HTTPS (port 443) so the agent can reach AWS API endpoints.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress \
     --group-id "$COMPUTE_SG_ID" \
     --protocol tcp \
     --port 443 \
     --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   <Aside type="tip">
     If `InvalidPermission.Duplicate` appears, the rule already exists. Continue to the next step.
   </Aside>

3. **Resolve the latest Amazon Linux 2023 AMI.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AMI_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-images \
     --owners amazon \
     --filters \
       "Name=name,Values=al2023-ami-*-kernel-*-x86_64" \
       "Name=virtualization-type,Values=hvm" \
       "Name=architecture,Values=x86_64" \
     --query 'sort_by(Images, &CreationDate)[-1].ImageId' \
     --output text \
     --region "$AWS_REGION")
   echo "AMI_ID=$AMI_ID"
   ```

4. **Choose a subnet for the instance.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   The subnet must be in the **same AZ as one of your mount targets** and have outbound internet access (via IGW or NAT) for SSM.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export INSTANCE_SUBNET_ID=subnet-0123456789abcdef0   # ← replace with your subnet ID
   echo "INSTANCE_SUBNET_ID=$INSTANCE_SUBNET_ID"
   ```

5. **Launch the EC2 instance.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export INSTANCE_ID=$(aws ec2 run-instances \
     --image-id "$AMI_ID" \
     --instance-type t3.micro \
     --subnet-id "$INSTANCE_SUBNET_ID" \
     --iam-instance-profile Name=s3files-ec2-instance-profile \
     --security-group-ids "$COMPUTE_SG_ID" \
     --metadata-options "HttpTokens=required,HttpEndpoint=enabled,HttpPutResponseHopLimit=2" \
     --tag-specifications "ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=s3files-demo-ec2}]" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'Instances[0].InstanceId' \
     --output text)
   echo "INSTANCE_ID=$INSTANCE_ID"
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     `HttpPutResponseHopLimit=2` is required when using IMDSv2 inside a container or with tools that need an extra hop. It is safe to set on bare EC2 instances as well.
   </Aside>

6. **Wait for the instance to reach running state.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws ec2 wait instance-running \
     --instance-ids "$INSTANCE_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   echo "Instance running"
   ```

7. **Wait for SSM registration.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   The SSM agent installed on Amazon Linux 2023 registers automatically within about 60 seconds. Poll until the instance appears:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   until aws ssm describe-instance-information \
     --filters "Key=InstanceIds,Values=$INSTANCE_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'InstanceInformationList[0].InstanceId' \
     --output text 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^i-"; do
     echo "Waiting for SSM registration…"
     sleep 15
   done
   echo "SSM registered"
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     If the loop runs longer than 3 minutes, confirm that:
     - The instance subnet has outbound HTTPS (port 443) — check step 2 and the subnet route table.
     - The instance profile `s3files-ec2-instance-profile` has `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` attached (added in [IAM](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/iam/)).
   </Aside>

8. **Open an SSM session.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws ssm start-session \
     --target "$INSTANCE_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   You are now in a shell on the instance as `ssm-user`. Continue to [Mount](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/mount/).

</Steps>

Run all commands in this page **inside the SSM session on the EC2 instance**. Start a session from your workstation if not already connected:

<Steps>

1. **Install `amazon-efs-utils` v3.0.0 or newer.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   S3 Files requires the updated `amazon-efs-utils` package that ships with the `s3files` mount type support. Run on the instance:

   ```bash frame="terminal"

   ```

   Confirm the installed version is 3.0.0 or newer:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   rpm -q amazon-efs-utils
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     The `mount -t s3files` helper is only available in `amazon-efs-utils` **v3.0.0+**. Earlier versions ship with EFS-only support. If the `dnf` version is too old, update the package index first: `sudo dnf update -y amazon-efs-utils`.
   </Aside>

2. **Set the file system ID in the session.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Export `FS_ID` inside the SSM session so the mount command can reference it:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export FS_ID=fs-0123456789abcdef0   # ← replace with the ID from Setup
   ```

   <Aside type="tip">
     Your `FS_ID` was printed during [File System](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/filesystem/) setup. If you have lost it, run the following **on your workstation** (not in the SSM session):

     ```bash frame="terminal"
       --region "$AWS_REGION" \
       --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
       --output text
     ```

3. **Create the mount point.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   sudo mkdir -p /mnt/s3files
   ```

4. **Mount the file system.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   sudo mount -t s3files "${FS_ID}:/" /mnt/s3files
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
     | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
   ```

## Overview

Lambda cannot mount an S3 Files file system directly by file system ID — an **access point** is required. The access point sets the root directory the function sees at `/mnt/s3files` and the POSIX identity under which files are created.

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}

   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --bucket "$BUCKET_ARN" \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)
   echo "FS_ID=$FS_ID"
   ```

   `FS_ID` must be `fs-…`. If it is `None`, complete [File System](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/filesystem/) first.

2. **Create the access point.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AP_ARN=$(aws s3files create-access-point \
     --file-system-id "$FS_ID" \
     --client-token "lambda-ap-$(date +%s)" \
     --posix-user "Uid=1000,Gid=1000" \
     --root-directory "Path=/lambda,CreationInfo={OwnerUid=1000,OwnerGid=1000,Permissions=755}" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'accessPoint.accessPointArn' \
     --output text)
   echo "AP_ARN=$AP_ARN"
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     `--client-token` ensures idempotency. If you re-run this command with the same token, the existing access point is returned rather than creating a duplicate.
   </Aside>

3. **Resolve the access point ID.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AP_ID=$(aws s3files list-access-points \
     --file-system-id "$FS_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'accessPoints[0].accessPointId' \
     --output text)
   echo "AP_ID=$AP_ID"
   ```

4. **Confirm the access point is available.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files list-access-points \
     --file-system-id "$FS_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'accessPoints[*].{Id:accessPointId,State:lifeCycleState,Root:rootDirectory.path}' \
     --output table
   ```

   The `State` column must show `available`.

</Steps>

## Overview

This page creates a simple Python Lambda function, configures it to run inside the VPC, and mounts the S3 file system at `/mnt/s3files` using the access point from the previous step.

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports and resolve the Lambda role ARN.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   export VPC_ID=vpc-0123456789abcdef0     # ← replace with your VPC ID
   export FUNCTION_NAME=s3files-demo

   # Resolve the Lambda role ARN by name
   export LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN=$(aws iam get-role \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-lambda \
     --query 'Role.Arn' \
     --output text)
   echo "LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN=$LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN"
   ```

2. **Resolve the compute security group and choose a subnet.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   The Lambda function must be in the same VPC as the mount targets. Use the compute security group from [Security Groups](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/security-groups/) which already has the NFS egress rule to the mount target SG.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export COMPUTE_SG_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups \
     --filters \
       "Name=group-name,Values=s3files-lambda-compute-sg" \
       "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' \
     --output text)
   echo "COMPUTE_SG_ID=$COMPUTE_SG_ID"

   export LAMBDA_SUBNET_ID=subnet-0123456789abcdef0   # ← subnet in the same AZ as a mount target
   echo "LAMBDA_SUBNET_ID=$LAMBDA_SUBNET_ID"
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     The Lambda subnet must have a route to the mount targets on **port 2049 TCP**. A private subnet behind a NAT gateway (for HTTPS to Lambda APIs) works well. A subnet with an internet gateway route also works.
   </Aside>

3. **Attach `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole` to the Lambda role.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   This allows Lambda to create and manage the ENI needed to run inside a VPC:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam attach-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-lambda \
     --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole
   ```

4. **Package the Lambda function code.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Create a simple Python handler that lists the mounted file system:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   mkdir -p /tmp/lambda-s3files

   cat > /tmp/lambda-s3files/index.py <<'EOF'
   import os

   def handler(event, context):
       path = '/mnt/s3files'
       try:
           entries = os.listdir(path)
           print(f"Contents of {path}: {entries}")
           return {'statusCode': 200, 'body': str(entries)}
       except Exception as e:
           return {'statusCode': 500, 'body': str(e)}
   EOF

   cd /tmp/lambda-s3files && zip lambda.zip index.py
   ```

5. **Create the Lambda function with VPC configuration.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda create-function \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --runtime python3.12 \
     --role "$LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN" \
     --handler index.handler \
     --zip-file fileb:///tmp/lambda-s3files/lambda.zip \
     --timeout 30 \
     --vpc-config "SubnetIds=${LAMBDA_SUBNET_ID},SecurityGroupIds=${COMPUTE_SG_ID}" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   Wait for the function to become active:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda wait function-active \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   echo "Function active"
   ```

6. **Attach the access point (file system config).** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   If `AP_ARN` is not still set in your shell, resolve it:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}

   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --bucket "$BUCKET_ARN" \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)

   export AP_ARN=$(aws s3files list-access-points \
     --file-system-id "$FS_ID" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query 'accessPoints[0].accessPointArn' \
     --output text)
   echo "AP_ARN=$AP_ARN"
   ```

   Update the function with the file system config:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda update-function-configuration \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --file-system-configs "Arn=${AP_ARN},LocalMountPath=/mnt/s3files" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"

   aws lambda wait function-updated \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   echo "File system config attached"
   ```

7. **Verify the function configuration.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda get-function-configuration \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --query '{State:State,VpcId:VpcConfig.VpcId,FileSystem:FileSystemConfigs[0].Arn}' \
     --output table
   ```

   `State` must be `Active`, and `FileSystem` must show the access point ARN.

</Steps>

## Overview

Invoke the function and read the JSON response to confirm the file system is mounted and accessible at `/mnt/s3files`.

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export FUNCTION_NAME=s3files-demo
   ```

2. **Invoke the function.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda invoke \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --payload '{}' \
     /tmp/lambda-response.json \
   && cat /tmp/lambda-response.json
   ```

   Expected response:

   ```json
   {"statusCode": 200, "body": "[]"}
   ```

   An empty list `[]` is correct for a newly created file system. The function successfully listed `/mnt/s3files`.

   <Aside type="note">
     If the first invocation returns a **timeout** or **mount error**, the mount target may still be establishing the NFS connection. Wait 60 seconds and retry. Cold-start Lambda invocations with VPC + file system configs can take 10–30 seconds on the first call.

     If the response body contains `[Errno 13] Permission denied`, the access point POSIX UID/GID (1000) does not match the file system root permissions.      --content-type text/plain \
   ```bash frame="terminal"
     --region "$AWS_REGION" <<< "hello from lambda walkthrough"
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws lambda invoke \
     --function-name "$FUNCTION_NAME" \
     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
     --payload '{}' \
     /tmp/lambda-response.json \
   && cat /tmp/lambda-response.json
   ```

   The response body should now list `['hello.txt']`.

4. **Check CloudWatch Logs.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws logs tail \
     "/aws/lambda/${FUNCTION_NAME}" \
     --since 5m \
     --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   Look for a log line like `Contents of /mnt/s3files: ['hello.txt']`.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   ```

2. **Create the bucket.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api create-bucket \
     --bucket $BUCKET \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=$AWS_REGION
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     If your region is `us-east-1`, omit `--create-bucket-configuration` — that region does not accept a `LocationConstraint`.
   </Aside>

3. **Enable versioning.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   S3 Files will fail to create a file system if versioning is not enabled.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
     --bucket $BUCKET \
     --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
   ```

   Verify:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket $BUCKET
   ```

   Expected output:

   ```json
   {
     "Status": "Enabled"
   }
   ```

4. **Confirm encryption.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   New buckets default to SSE-S3 (AES-256). Verify:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket $BUCKET
   ```

   The rule type must be `aws:kms` (SSE-KMS) or `AES256` (SSE-S3). If the command returns a `ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError`, apply SSE-S3 explicitly:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \
     --bucket $BUCKET \
     --server-side-encryption-configuration '{
       "Rules": [{
         "ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {
           "SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"
         }
       }]
     }'
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     SSE-C (customer-provided keys) and DSSE-KMS are **not supported** by S3 Files. Using an unsupported encryption type will cause file system creation to fail.
   </Aside>

5. **Seed the `demo/` prefix.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Upload a single synthetic text object at `demo/walkthrough.txt`. The EC2 mount walkthrough uses that key for read checks (`cat`, `aws s3 cp`, greps). The script builds the file with `echo` lines (no heredoc) to avoid paste-terminator issues.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   DEMO_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
   WALK="$DEMO_ROOT/walkthrough.txt"

   {
     echo 'S3 Files walkthrough — demo fixture'
     echo '==================================='
     echo ''
     echo 'This is the one shared object for all demo scenarios in this documentation set.'
     echo 'Use it to confirm reads through the mount (cat, less, editors) and via the'
     echo 'AWS CLI (aws s3 cp) with a short but non-trivial body of text.'
     echo ''
     echo 'Canonical marker (for greps): DEMO_BUNDLE_VERSION=1'
   } > "$WALK"

   aws s3 cp "$WALK" "s3://$BUCKET/demo/walkthrough.txt" --region "$AWS_REGION"
   rm -rf "$DEMO_ROOT"
   ```

   Confirm the upload:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3 ls "s3://$BUCKET/demo/" --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   You should see `demo/walkthrough.txt`.

</Steps>

## Overview

The <Tooltip term="s3files" /> file system links your bucket to a mountable NFS endpoint. Before creating it you must create the IAM role S3 Files assumes to read and write your bucket — both steps are on this page.

<Aside type="caution">
  If `aws s3files` fails with `Found invalid choice 's3files'`, your AWS CLI v2 is below **2.34.26**, or you are on **AWS CLI v1** (for example from `pip`). Run `aws --version` and `aws s3files help` to confirm you meet the minimum version before continuing.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell. **Replace `my-s3-files-bucket` with the exact name of the bucket you created in the Bucket step** — this value is embedded in the IAM policy resource ARNs written in steps 2–3. Using the wrong name here is the most common cause of the file system getting stuck in `creating`.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   echo "Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  Region: $AWS_REGION  Bucket: $BUCKET  ARN: $BUCKET_ARN"
   ```

   Confirm the echo output shows your real bucket name (not the placeholder) before continuing.

   If the bucket does not exist yet, complete [Bucket](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/bucket/) first.

2. **Create the IAM role S3 Files assumes (trust policy).** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   This role allows **`elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com`** to assume it, scoped to this account and region. The heredoc uses **unquoted** `<<EOF` so the shell expands `${ACCOUNT_ID}` and `${AWS_REGION}` — do not use `<<'EOF'`.

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="fs-trust-policy.json"
   cat > /tmp/fs-trust-policy.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "AllowS3FilesAssumeRole",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": { "Service": "elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com" },
       "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
       "Condition": {
         "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "${ACCOUNT_ID}" },
         "ArnLike": {
           "aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:s3files:${AWS_REGION}:${ACCOUNT_ID}:file-system/*"
         }
       }
     }]
   }
   EOF
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam create-role \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --assume-role-policy-document file:///tmp/fs-trust-policy.json
   ```

   Verify the trust policy expanded correctly — you must see your account ID digits and region code, not literal `${ACCOUNT_ID}`:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam get-role \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --query 'Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument' \
     --output json
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     **Trust policy `aws:SourceArn` must use the `s3files` ARN, not `elasticfilesystem`.** The **principal** is `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com`, but the **condition** must match how AWS identifies S3 Files file systems: `arn:aws:s3files:REGION:ACCOUNT_ID:file-system/*`. If you use `arn:aws:elasticfilesystem:…:file-system/*` (a common mistake when reusing EFS examples), assume-role or sync can fail and the console may show **Unknown Error** on **Synchronization configuration** even when the file system reaches `available`. Fix with `update-assume-role-policy` using the JSON from this step, then wait briefly and refresh the console.
   </Aside>

   <Aside type="note">
     If the role already exists from a previous attempt, skip `create-role` and go straight to the next step to re-apply the inline policy.
   </Aside>

3. **Attach the file system inline policy (S3, KMS, EventBridge).** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   This grants S3 Files read/write access to the bucket, optional SSE-KMS key use, and EventBridge sync rule management, following the [AWS prerequisites for S3 Files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-files-prereq-policies.html#s3-files-prereq-iam-creation-role).

   <Aside type="note">
     If the bucket uses **SSE-S3 only**, remove the `UseKmsKeyWithS3Files` statement before running `put-role-policy` — it is only required for **SSE-KMS** buckets.
   </Aside>

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="fs-inline-policy.json"
   cat > /tmp/fs-inline-policy.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Sid": "S3BucketPermissions",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["s3:ListBucket", "s3:ListBucketVersions"],
         "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}",
         "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:ResourceAccount": "${ACCOUNT_ID}" } }
       },
      {
        "Sid": "S3ObjectPermissions",
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["s3:AbortMultipartUpload", "s3:DeleteObject*", "s3:GetObject*", "s3:HeadObject", "s3:List*", "s3:PutObject*"],
        "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}/*",
        "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:ResourceAccount": "${ACCOUNT_ID}" } }
      },
       {
         "Sid": "UseKmsKeyWithS3Files",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncryptFrom", "kms:ReEncryptTo"],
         "Condition": {
           "StringLike": {
             "kms:ViaService": "s3.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com",
             "kms:EncryptionContext:aws:s3:arn": ["${BUCKET_ARN}", "${BUCKET_ARN}/*"]
           }
         },
         "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${AWS_REGION}:${ACCOUNT_ID}:*"
       },
       {
         "Sid": "EventBridgeManage",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["events:DeleteRule", "events:DisableRule", "events:EnableRule", "events:PutRule", "events:PutTargets", "events:RemoveTargets"],
         "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "events:ManagedBy": "elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com" } },
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:events:*:*:rule/DO-NOT-DELETE-S3-Files*"]
       },
       {
         "Sid": "EventBridgeRead",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["events:DescribeRule", "events:ListRuleNamesByTarget", "events:ListRules", "events:ListTargetsByRule"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:events:*:*:rule/*"]
       }
     ]
   }
   EOF
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam put-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --policy-name S3FilesFileSystemPolicy \
     --policy-document file:///tmp/fs-inline-policy.json
   ```

4. **Verify the file system role is ready.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam get-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --policy-name S3FilesFileSystemPolicy \
     --query 'PolicyDocument.Statement[0:2]' \
     --output json
   ```

   Check that both `Resource` values contain your **real bucket name**, not `my-s3-files-bucket`:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam get-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --policy-name S3FilesFileSystemPolicy \
     --query 'PolicyDocument.Statement[*].Resource' \
     --output text
   ```

   If you see `my-s3-files-bucket` in the output, stop. Re-run step 1 with the correct `BUCKET=` value, re-run step 3 (`put-role-policy`), then re-run this verification before continuing.

5. **Set the file system role ARN.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export FS_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::${ACCOUNT_ID}:role/s3files-filesystem-role
   echo "FS_ROLE_ARN=$FS_ROLE_ARN"
   ```

6. **Create the file system.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files create-file-system \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
     --role-arn $FS_ROLE_ARN
   ```

   The response is JSON. Note the `fileSystemId` value — it starts with `fs-`.

   <Aside type="note">
     **What to expect in the AWS Console while the file system is `Creating`:**

     - **"This file system doesn't have any mount targets"** — expected; mount targets are created in the next setup page.
     - **"Unknown Error" in the Synchronization configuration panel** — often **transient** while status is still `Creating`. Once the file system is **`available`**, this panel should load. If **Unknown Error persists after `available`**, open the **API response** details in the banner: it is usually an IAM permission issue on the **file system role** (wrong trust `aws:SourceArn`, or EventBridge statements that do not match [AWS prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-files-prereq-policies.html) — manage actions must target `DO-NOT-DELETE-S3-Files*` with `events:ManagedBy`, not a generic `s3-files-*` pattern). Re-apply steps 2–3, then refresh.
   </Aside>

   <Aside type="caution">
     **If `create-file-system` returns "Access denied: S3 Files does not have permissions to assume the provided role"** — the trust policy is wrong. Common causes: heredoc written with `<<'EOF'` (variables not expanded), or `AWS_REGION`/`ACCOUNT_ID` were unset in step 2, or **`aws:SourceArn` uses `arn:aws:elasticfilesystem:…` instead of `arn:aws:s3files:…`** (see the caution under step 2). Fix: re-run step 1, regenerate `/tmp/fs-trust-policy.json`, run `aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name s3files-filesystem-role --policy-document file:///tmp/fs-trust-policy.json`, then retry `create-file-system`.

     **If the file system is stuck in `Creating` with `statusMessage: "Access denied: ... s3:HeadObject"`** — the inline policy resource ARN points to the wrong bucket (the placeholder was not replaced). Fix without deleting the file system: re-run step 1 with the correct `BUCKET=` value, re-run step 3 (`put-role-policy`), then wait ~60 seconds — the file system will automatically retry and transition to `available`.

     Check status and `statusMessage` **before** you export `FS_ID` in step 7 — use your bucket (same variables as `create-file-system`), not `$FS_ID`:
     ```bash frame="terminal"
     aws s3files list-file-systems \
       --region $AWS_REGION \
       --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
       --query 'fileSystems[0].{id:fileSystemId,status:status,message:statusMessage}' \
       --output json
     ```
     After step 7 sets `FS_ID`, you can use `aws s3files get-file-system --file-system-id $FS_ID` instead.
   </Aside>

7. **Export the file system ID.**

   The S3 Files API uses **`list-file-systems`** and **`get-file-system`**, not `describe-file-systems`. Scope the list to your bucket so the query stays unambiguous if you have multiple file systems:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)
   echo "File system: $FS_ID"
   ```

8. **Wait for the file system to become available.**

   File system creation typically completes within one to two minutes. Re-run until the output is `available`:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files get-file-system \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --query 'status' \
     --output text
   ```

   Once the output is `available`, the console's Synchronization configuration "Unknown Error" and the "no mount targets" warning both clear — no action required.

</Steps>

## Overview

A <Tooltip term="mount-target" /> gives compute resources a network path to the file system within a single <Tooltip term="az" />. Create one per AZ where your EC2 instances run — you can have at most one per AZ.

<Aside type="note">
  On [EC2 — Launch & install](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/install-client/), the instance subnet can differ from **`SUBNET_ID_AZA`** here as long as it stays in the **same Availability Zone** — that lets Session Manager use a subnet with internet egress while mount targets remain on private subnets.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell so all required variables are set:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)
   echo "Region: $AWS_REGION  Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  FS: $FS_ID"
   ```

   If `FS_ID` is empty or `None`, complete [File System](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/filesystem/) first.

2. **List your VPC subnets and identify one per AZ.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export VPC_ID=vpc-0123456789abcdef0   # replace with your VPC ID

   aws ec2 describe-subnets \
     --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" \
     --query 'Subnets[*].{AZ:AvailabilityZone,SubnetId:SubnetId,CIDR:CidrBlock}' \
     --output table \
     --region $AWS_REGION
   ```

   Note a subnet ID for each AZ you need. Pick the private subnets where your EC2 instances will run.

3. **Create a security group for mount targets.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export MT_SG_ID=$(aws ec2 create-security-group \
     --group-name s3files-mount-target-sg \
     --description "S3 Files mount target - NFS inbound" \
     --vpc-id $VPC_ID \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --query GroupId \
     --output text)
   echo "Mount target SG: $MT_SG_ID"
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     The inbound NFS rule (port 2049) is added in the [Security Groups](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/security-groups/) step after you know the compute security group ID.
   </Aside>

4. **Create a mount target in each AZ.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   From the step 2 table, copy **one subnet ID per Availability Zone** where you need NFS. Assign each to a shell variable **before** calling `create-mount-target`.

   **First AZ (required):** set a real subnet ID. Match the AZ column from step 2 in the comment:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export SUBNET_ID_AZA=subnet-0123456789abcdef0   # replace — e.g. private subnet in ap-southeast-6a
   ```

   **Second AZ (required if your VPC has a second AZ and you want HA):**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export SUBNET_ID_AZB=subnet-0fedcba9876543210   # replace — e.g. private subnet in ap-southeast-6b
   ```

   Add another `export SUBNET_ID_AZC=subnet-…` for each extra AZ — do not run `create-mount-target` with placeholder subnet IDs.

   <Aside type="note">
     Bash treats **`SUBNET_ID_AZA`** and **`SUBNET_ID_AZa`** as different variables. Use **all-uppercase** `AZA` / `AZB` / `AZC` in both `export` and `$SUBNET_ID_…` references, or `--subnet-id` can end up empty and the CLI returns `expected one argument`.
   </Aside>

   Create one mount target per export (at most one mount target per AZ):

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files create-mount-target \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --subnet-id $SUBNET_ID_AZA \
     --security-groups $MT_SG_ID

   aws s3files create-mount-target \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --subnet-id $SUBNET_ID_AZB \
     --security-groups $MT_SG_ID
   ```

   If you only use **one** AZ, keep the first `export` and the first `create-mount-target` only; skip `SUBNET_ID_AZB` and the second API call.

   Mount target creation takes up to 5 minutes per target.

5. **Wait until all mount targets are available.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files list-mount-targets \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --query 'mountTargets[*].{AZ:availabilityZoneId,State:status,IP:ipv4Address}' \
     --output table
   ```

   Re-run until all entries show `available` in the State column.

</Steps>

## Overview

<Tooltip term="s3files" /> requires exactly two <Tooltip term="iam" /> roles:

| Role | Who assumes it | Purpose |
| ---- | -------------- | ------- |
| **File system role** | `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com` | S3 Files reads/writes the bucket and manages EventBridge sync rules |
| **Compute role** | EC2 instance profile | EC2 mounts the file system and reads objects directly from S3 |

The **file system** role was created in [File System](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/filesystem/). This page creates the **EC2 compute** role.

<Aside type="caution">
  The file system role principal is `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com` — not `s3.amazonaws.com`. This is intentional; S3 Files is built on EFS infrastructure.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell so all required variables are set:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   echo "Region: $AWS_REGION  Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  Bucket ARN: $BUCKET_ARN"
   ```

2. **Create the EC2 compute role.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Role name **`s3files-compute-role-ec2`**, instance profile **`s3files-ec2-instance-profile`**.

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="compute-trust-ec2.json"
   cat > /tmp/compute-trust-ec2.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [{
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": { "Service": "ec2.amazonaws.com" },
       "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
     }]
   }
   EOF
   aws iam create-role \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-ec2 \
     --assume-role-policy-document file:///tmp/compute-trust-ec2.json
   ```

3. **Attach managed policies.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Attach **`AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess`** to allow mounting the file system:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam attach-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-ec2 \
     --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess
   ```

   Attach **`AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`** so the instance can register with Systems Manager — required for the [EC2 launch walkthrough](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/install-client/) (Session Manager shell, no SSH):

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam attach-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-ec2 \
     --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore
   ```

4. **Attach an inline S3 read policy.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="compute-s3-read-ec2.json"
   cat > /tmp/compute-s3-read-ec2.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Sid": "S3ObjectReadAccess",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:GetObjectVersion"],
         "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}/*"
       },
       {
         "Sid": "S3BucketListAccess",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": "s3:ListBucket",
         "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}"
       }
     ]
   }
   EOF
   aws iam put-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-ec2 \
     --policy-name S3FilesComputeS3ReadPolicy \
     --policy-document file:///tmp/compute-s3-read-ec2.json
   ```

5. **Create the instance profile and add the role.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name s3files-ec2-instance-profile
   ```

<Tooltip term="s3files" /> uses <Tooltip term="nfs" /> over port 2049 TCP. This page **creates** the EC2 compute security group **`s3files-ec2-compute-sg`**, stores its ID in **`COMPUTE_SG_ID`**, and adds the paired rules with **`MT_SG_ID`** from [Mount Targets](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/mount-targets/). <Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell. Replace `VPC_ID` with your VPC; `MT_SG_ID` is looked up by name from the group created in [Mount Targets](/s3-files-workloads/ec2/setup/mount-targets/).

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export VPC_ID=vpc-0123456789abcdef0   # replace with your VPC ID

   export MT_SG_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-security-groups \
     --filters "Name=group-name,Values=s3files-mount-target-sg" \
               "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' \
     --output text)
   echo "MT_SG_ID=$MT_SG_ID"
   ```

2. **Create the compute security group and capture its ID.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Fixed name **`s3files-ec2-compute-sg`** so the rest of the EC2 walkthrough can resolve **`COMPUTE_SG_ID`** without placeholders.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export COMPUTE_SG_ID=$(aws ec2 create-security-group \
     --group-name s3files-ec2-compute-sg \
     --description "S3 Files EC2 walkthrough - compute (NFS to mount targets; Session Manager)" \
     --vpc-id $VPC_ID \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --query GroupId \
     --output text)
   echo "COMPUTE_SG_ID=$COMPUTE_SG_ID"
   ```

   <Aside type="tip">
     If **`Resource.AlreadyExists`** appears, the group already exists. Resolve the ID instead:  
     `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters "Name=group-name,Values=s3files-ec2-compute-sg" "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" --region $AWS_REGION --query 'SecurityGroups[0].GroupId' --output text`

3. **Allow outbound NFS from the compute security group.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
     --group-id $COMPUTE_SG_ID \
     --protocol tcp \
     --port 2049 \
     --source-group $MT_SG_ID \
     --region $AWS_REGION
   ```

4. **Allow inbound NFS on the mount target security group.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
     --group-id $MT_SG_ID \
     --protocol tcp \
     --port 2049 \
     --source-group $COMPUTE_SG_ID \
     --region $AWS_REGION
   ```

5. **Verify the rules.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
     --filters "Name=group-id,Values=$COMPUTE_SG_ID" \

     --output table \
     --region $AWS_REGION
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws ec2 describe-security-group-rules \
     --filters "Name=group-id,Values=$MT_SG_ID" \
     --query 'SecurityGroupRules[?IsEgress==`false` && ToPort==`2049`].{Port:ToPort,Source:ReferencedGroupInfo.GroupId}' \
     --output table \
     --region $AWS_REGION
   ```

   Both queries should return one row each showing port `2049` and the correct SG reference.

## Overview

<Tooltip term="s3files" /> requires <Tooltip term="versioning" /> to synchronise changes between the file system and the bucket. It also supports only <Tooltip term="sse" /> — specifically SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS. Set both before creating the file system.

<Steps>

1. **Set environment variables.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Use these exports throughout the Lambda walkthrough. Replace values to match your environment.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   echo "Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  Region: $AWS_REGION  Bucket: $BUCKET"
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     S3 bucket names are **globally unique** across all AWS accounts. If `my-s3-files-bucket` is already taken, `create-bucket` in the next step will fail with `BucketAlreadyExists`. Choose a name that is unique — for example prefix it with your account ID: `$ACCOUNT_ID-s3files-bucket`.
   </Aside>

2. **Create the bucket.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api create-bucket \
     --bucket $BUCKET \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=$AWS_REGION
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     If your region is `us-east-1`, omit `--create-bucket-configuration` — that region does not accept a `LocationConstraint`.
   </Aside>

3. **Enable versioning.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   S3 Files will fail to create a file system if versioning is not enabled.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
     --bucket $BUCKET \
     --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
   ```

   Verify:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket $BUCKET
   ```

   Expected output:

   ```json
   {
     "Status": "Enabled"
   }
   ```

4. **Confirm encryption.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   New buckets default to SSE-S3 (AES-256). Verify:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket $BUCKET
   ```

   The rule type must be `aws:kms` (SSE-KMS) or `AES256` (SSE-S3). If the command returns a `ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError`, apply SSE-S3 explicitly:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3api put-bucket-encryption \
     --bucket $BUCKET \
     --server-side-encryption-configuration '{
       "Rules": [{
         "ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {
           "SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"
         }
       }]
     }'
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     SSE-C (customer-provided keys) and DSSE-KMS are **not supported** by S3 Files. Using an unsupported encryption type will cause file system creation to fail.
   </Aside>

5. **Seed the `lambda/` prefix.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   The Lambda access point is configured with root directory `Path=/lambda`. The function can only see objects under that prefix. Seed a fixture file so the mount is not empty on first invocation.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   printf 'Hello from S3 Files Lambda walkthrough\n' \
     | aws s3 cp - "s3://$BUCKET/lambda/hello.txt" --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   Confirm the upload:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3 ls "s3://$BUCKET/lambda/" --region "$AWS_REGION"
   ```

   You should see `lambda/hello.txt`.

   <Aside type="note">
     Lambda mounts an access point whose root directory is `Path=/lambda`, so function reads and writes land under the `lambda/` key prefix in the bucket. Objects outside `lambda/` are not visible through the mount.
   </Aside>

</Steps>

## Overview

The <Tooltip term="s3files" /> file system links your bucket to a mountable NFS endpoint. Before creating it you must create the IAM role S3 Files assumes to read and write your bucket — both steps are on this page.

<Aside type="caution">
  If `aws s3files` fails with `Found invalid choice 's3files'`, your AWS CLI v2 is below **2.34.26**, or you are on **AWS CLI v1** (for example from `pip`). Run `aws --version` and `aws s3files help` to confirm you meet the minimum version before continuing.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell. **Replace `my-s3-files-bucket` with the exact name of the bucket you created in the Bucket step** — this value is embedded in the IAM policy resource ARNs written in steps 2–3. Using the wrong name here is the most common cause of the file system getting stuck in `creating`.

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   echo "Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  Region: $AWS_REGION  Bucket: $BUCKET  ARN: $BUCKET_ARN"
   ```

   Confirm the echo output shows your real bucket name (not the placeholder) before continuing.

   If the bucket does not exist yet, complete [Bucket](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/bucket/) first.

2. **Create the IAM role S3 Files assumes (trust policy).** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   This role allows **`elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com`** to assume it, scoped to this account and region. The heredoc uses **unquoted** `<<EOF` so the shell expands `${ACCOUNT_ID}` and `${AWS_REGION}` — do not use `<<'EOF'`.

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="fs-trust-policy.json"
   cat > /tmp/fs-trust-policy.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [{
       "Sid": "AllowS3FilesAssumeRole",
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": { "Service": "elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com" },
       "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
       "Condition": {
         "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "${ACCOUNT_ID}" },
         "ArnLike": {
           "aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:s3files:${AWS_REGION}:${ACCOUNT_ID}:file-system/*"
         }
       }
     }]
   }
   EOF
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam create-role \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --assume-role-policy-document file:///tmp/fs-trust-policy.json
   ```

   Verify the trust policy expanded correctly — you must see your account ID digits and region code, not literal `${ACCOUNT_ID}`:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam get-role \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --query 'Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument' \
     --output json
   ```

   <Aside type="caution">
     **Trust policy `aws:SourceArn` must use the `s3files` ARN, not `elasticfilesystem`.** The **principal** is `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com`, but the **condition** must match how AWS identifies S3 Files file systems: `arn:aws:s3files:REGION:ACCOUNT_ID:file-system/*`. If you use `arn:aws:elasticfilesystem:…:file-system/*` (a common mistake when reusing EFS examples), assume-role or sync can fail and the console may show **Unknown Error** on **Synchronization configuration** even when the file system reaches `available`. Fix with `update-assume-role-policy` using the JSON from this step, then wait briefly and refresh the console.
   </Aside>

   <Aside type="note">
     If the role already exists from a previous attempt, skip `create-role` and go straight to the next step to re-apply the inline policy.
   </Aside>

3. **Attach the file system inline policy (S3, KMS, EventBridge).** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   This grants S3 Files read/write access to the bucket, optional SSE-KMS key use, and EventBridge sync rule management, following the [AWS prerequisites for S3 Files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-files-prereq-policies.html#s3-files-prereq-iam-creation-role).

   <Aside type="note">
     If the bucket uses **SSE-S3 only**, remove the `UseKmsKeyWithS3Files` statement before running `put-role-policy` — it is only required for **SSE-KMS** buckets.
   </Aside>

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="fs-inline-policy.json"
   cat > /tmp/fs-inline-policy.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Sid": "S3BucketPermissions",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["s3:ListBucket", "s3:ListBucketVersions"],
         "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}",
         "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:ResourceAccount": "${ACCOUNT_ID}" } }
       },
      {
        "Sid": "S3ObjectPermissions",
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Action": ["s3:AbortMultipartUpload", "s3:DeleteObject*", "s3:GetObject*", "s3:HeadObject", "s3:List*", "s3:PutObject*"],
        "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}/*",
        "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:ResourceAccount": "${ACCOUNT_ID}" } }
      },
       {
         "Sid": "UseKmsKeyWithS3Files",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Encrypt", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncryptFrom", "kms:ReEncryptTo"],
         "Condition": {
           "StringLike": {
             "kms:ViaService": "s3.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com",
             "kms:EncryptionContext:aws:s3:arn": ["${BUCKET_ARN}", "${BUCKET_ARN}/*"]
           }
         },
         "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${AWS_REGION}:${ACCOUNT_ID}:*"
       },
       {
         "Sid": "EventBridgeManage",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["events:DeleteRule", "events:DisableRule", "events:EnableRule", "events:PutRule", "events:PutTargets", "events:RemoveTargets"],
         "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "events:ManagedBy": "elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com" } },
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:events:*:*:rule/DO-NOT-DELETE-S3-Files*"]
       },
       {
         "Sid": "EventBridgeRead",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["events:DescribeRule", "events:ListRuleNamesByTarget", "events:ListRules", "events:ListTargetsByRule"],
         "Resource": ["arn:aws:events:*:*:rule/*"]
       }
     ]
   }
   EOF
   ```

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam put-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --policy-name S3FilesFileSystemPolicy \
     --policy-document file:///tmp/fs-inline-policy.json
   ```

4. **Verify the file system role is ready.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam get-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --policy-name S3FilesFileSystemPolicy \
     --query 'PolicyDocument.Statement[0:2]' \
     --output json
   ```

   Check that both `Resource` values contain your **real bucket name**, not `my-s3-files-bucket`:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam get-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-filesystem-role \
     --policy-name S3FilesFileSystemPolicy \
     --query 'PolicyDocument.Statement[*].Resource' \
     --output text
   ```

   If you see `my-s3-files-bucket` in the output, stop. Re-run step 1 with the correct `BUCKET=` value, re-run step 3 (`put-role-policy`), then re-run this verification before continuing.

5. **Set the file system role ARN.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export FS_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::${ACCOUNT_ID}:role/s3files-filesystem-role
   echo "FS_ROLE_ARN=$FS_ROLE_ARN"
   ```

6. **Create the file system.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files create-file-system \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
     --role-arn $FS_ROLE_ARN
   ```

   The response is JSON. Note the `fileSystemId` value — it starts with `fs-`.

   <Aside type="note">
     **What to expect in the AWS Console while the file system is `Creating`:**

     - **"This file system doesn't have any mount targets"** — expected; mount targets are created in the next setup page.
     - **"Unknown Error" in the Synchronization configuration panel** — often **transient** while status is still `Creating`. Once the file system is **`available`**, this panel should load. If **Unknown Error persists after `available`**, open the **API response** details in the banner: it is usually an IAM permission issue on the **file system role** (wrong trust `aws:SourceArn`, or EventBridge statements that do not match [AWS prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-files-prereq-policies.html) — manage actions must target `DO-NOT-DELETE-S3-Files*` with `events:ManagedBy`, not a generic `s3-files-*` pattern). Re-apply steps 2–3, then refresh.
   </Aside>

   <Aside type="caution">
     **If `create-file-system` returns "Access denied: S3 Files does not have permissions to assume the provided role"** — the trust policy is wrong. Common causes: heredoc written with `<<'EOF'` (variables not expanded), or `AWS_REGION`/`ACCOUNT_ID` were unset in step 2, or **`aws:SourceArn` uses `arn:aws:elasticfilesystem:…` instead of `arn:aws:s3files:…`** (see the caution under step 2). Fix: re-run step 1, regenerate `/tmp/fs-trust-policy.json`, run `aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name s3files-filesystem-role --policy-document file:///tmp/fs-trust-policy.json`, then retry `create-file-system`.

     **If the file system is stuck in `Creating` with `statusMessage: "Access denied: ... s3:HeadObject"`** — the inline policy resource ARN points to the wrong bucket (the placeholder was not replaced). Fix without deleting the file system: re-run step 1 with the correct `BUCKET=` value, re-run step 3 (`put-role-policy`), then wait ~60 seconds — the file system will automatically retry and transition to `available`.

     Check status and `statusMessage` **before** you export `FS_ID` in step 7:
     ```bash frame="terminal"
     aws s3files list-file-systems \
       --region $AWS_REGION \
       --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
       --query 'fileSystems[0].{id:fileSystemId,status:status,message:statusMessage}' \
       --output json
     ```
     After step 7 sets `FS_ID`, you can use `aws s3files get-file-system --file-system-id $FS_ID` instead.
   </Aside>

7. **Export the file system ID.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)
   echo "File system: $FS_ID"
   ```

8. **Wait for the file system to become available.**

   File system creation typically completes within one to two minutes. Re-run until the output is `available`:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files get-file-system \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --query 'status' \
     --output text
   ```

   Once the output is `available`, the console's Synchronization configuration "Unknown Error" and the "no mount targets" warning both clear — no action required.

</Steps>

## Overview

A <Tooltip term="mount-target" /> gives compute resources a network path to the file system within a single <Tooltip term="az" />. Create one per AZ where your Lambda functions run — you can have at most one per AZ.

<Aside type="note">
  Lambda functions must be configured in the **same VPC** as the mount targets. The Lambda security group (created in [Security Groups](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/security-groups/)) must have outbound NFS (port 2049) to the mount target security group.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell so all required variables are set:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   export FS_ID=$(aws s3files list-file-systems \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --bucket $BUCKET_ARN \
     --query 'fileSystems[0].fileSystemId' \
     --output text)
   echo "Region: $AWS_REGION  Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  FS: $FS_ID"
   ```

   If `FS_ID` is empty or `None`, complete [File System](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/filesystem/) first.

2. **List your VPC subnets and identify one per AZ.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export VPC_ID=vpc-0123456789abcdef0   # replace with your VPC ID

   aws ec2 describe-subnets \
     --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" \
     --query 'Subnets[*].{AZ:AvailabilityZone,SubnetId:SubnetId,CIDR:CidrBlock}' \
     --output table \
     --region $AWS_REGION
   ```

   Note a subnet ID for each AZ you need. Pick the private subnets where your Lambda functions will run.

3. **Create a security group for mount targets.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export MT_SG_ID=$(aws ec2 create-security-group \
     --group-name s3files-mount-target-sg \
     --description "S3 Files mount target - NFS inbound" \
     --vpc-id $VPC_ID \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --query GroupId \
     --output text)
   echo "Mount target SG: $MT_SG_ID"
   ```

   <Aside type="note">
     The inbound NFS rule (port 2049) is added in the [Security Groups](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/security-groups/) step after you know the compute security group ID.
   </Aside>

4. **Create a mount target in each AZ.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   From the step 2 table, copy **one subnet ID per Availability Zone** where you need NFS. Assign each to a shell variable **before** calling `create-mount-target`.

   **First AZ (required):** set a real subnet ID:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export SUBNET_ID_AZA=subnet-0123456789abcdef0   # replace — e.g. private subnet in ap-southeast-6a
   ```

   **Second AZ (required if your VPC has a second AZ and you want HA):**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export SUBNET_ID_AZB=subnet-0fedcba9876543210   # replace — e.g. private subnet in ap-southeast-6b
   ```

   Add another `export SUBNET_ID_AZC=subnet-…` for each extra AZ — do not run `create-mount-target` with placeholder subnet IDs.

   <Aside type="note">
     Bash treats **`SUBNET_ID_AZA`** and **`SUBNET_ID_AZa`** as different variables. Use **all-uppercase** `AZA` / `AZB` / `AZC` in both `export` and `$SUBNET_ID_…` references, or `--subnet-id` can end up empty and the CLI returns `expected one argument`.
   </Aside>

   Create one mount target per export (at most one mount target per AZ):

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files create-mount-target \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --subnet-id $SUBNET_ID_AZA \
     --security-groups $MT_SG_ID

   aws s3files create-mount-target \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --subnet-id $SUBNET_ID_AZB \
     --security-groups $MT_SG_ID
   ```

   If you only use **one** AZ, keep the first `export` and the first `create-mount-target` only; skip `SUBNET_ID_AZB` and the second API call.

   Mount target creation takes up to 5 minutes per target.

5. **Wait until all mount targets are available.**

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws s3files list-mount-targets \
     --region $AWS_REGION \
     --file-system-id $FS_ID \
     --query 'mountTargets[*].{AZ:availabilityZoneId,State:status,IP:ipv4Address}' \
     --output table
   ```

   Re-run until all entries show `available` in the State column.

</Steps>

## Overview

<Tooltip term="s3files" /> requires exactly two <Tooltip term="iam" /> roles:

| Role | Who assumes it | Purpose |
| ---- | -------------- | ------- |
| **File system role** | `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com` | S3 Files reads/writes the bucket and manages EventBridge sync rules |
| **Compute role** | Lambda execution role | Lambda mounts the file system and reads objects directly from S3 |

The **file system** role was created in [File System](/s3-files-workloads/lambda/setup/filesystem/). This page creates the **Lambda execution** role.

<Aside type="caution">
  The file system role principal is `elasticfilesystem.amazonaws.com` — not `s3.amazonaws.com`. This is intentional; S3 Files is built on EFS infrastructure.
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Confirm base exports.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Re-run these in your current shell so all required variables are set:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   export AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-6
   export ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
   export BUCKET=my-s3-files-bucket        # ← replace with your real bucket name
   export BUCKET_ARN=arn:aws:s3:::${BUCKET}
   echo "Region: $AWS_REGION  Account: $ACCOUNT_ID  Bucket ARN: $BUCKET_ARN"
   ```

2. **Create the Lambda execution role.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Role name **`s3files-compute-role-lambda`** (execution role for the function).

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="compute-trust-lambda.json"
   cat > /tmp/compute-trust-lambda.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [{
       "Effect": "Allow",
       "Principal": { "Service": "lambda.amazonaws.com" },
       "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
     }]
   }
   EOF
   aws iam create-role \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-lambda \
     --assume-role-policy-document file:///tmp/compute-trust-lambda.json
   ```

3. **Attach managed policies.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   Attach **`AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess`** to allow mounting the file system:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam attach-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-lambda \
     --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FilesClientFullAccess
   ```

   Attach **`AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole`** to allow writing to CloudWatch Logs:

   ```bash frame="terminal"
   aws iam attach-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-lambda \
     --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
   ```

4. **Attach an inline S3 read policy.** <Badge text="Required" variant="tip" size="small" />

   ```bash frame="terminal" title="compute-s3-read-lambda.json"
   cat > /tmp/compute-s3-read-lambda.json <<EOF
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Sid": "S3ObjectReadAccess",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:GetObjectVersion"],
         "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}/*"
       },
       {
         "Sid": "S3BucketListAccess",
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": "s3:ListBucket",
         "Resource": "${BUCKET_ARN}"
       }
     ]
   }
   EOF
   aws iam put-role-policy \
     --role-name s3files-compute-role-lambda \
     --policy-name S3FilesComputeS3ReadPolicy \
     --policy-document file:///tmp/compute-s3-read-lambda.json
   ```

</Steps>
